issue.title: Decoder reuse in MediaSessionConnector

repository.name: ExoPlayer
repository.description: This project is deprecated and stale. The latest ExoPlayer code is available in https://github.com/androidx/media

issue.body:
### [REQUIRED] Searched documentation and issues
Recent [Improved decoder reuse in ExoPlayer](https://medium.com/google-exoplayer/improved-decoder-reuse-in-exoplayer-ef4c6d99591d) blog post explains how to make sure your app benefits from decoder reuse:

> When re-preparing the player with a different video, call prepare() with the new MediaSource without calling stop() first. This is because by default, ExoPlayer will still release decoders when stop() is called.

I noticed MediaSessionConnector.java calls [stopPlayerForPrepare(boolean playWhenReady) ](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/44293e8f45fc62ff918001b4425c44d0ded5ffc9/extensions/mediasession/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/ext/mediasession/MediaSessionConnector.java#L837)before preparing new source.

### [REQUIRED] Question
Is there a reason why MediaSessionConnector calls player.stop() before preparing new source? Is this not against best practices for decoder reuse?

body: Yep, that's wrong.  I'll provide a fix asap.

issue.title: `Play` Action from MediaSession not handled correctly after a `Pause` action

repository.name: ExoPlayer
repository.description: This project is deprecated and stale. The latest ExoPlayer code is available in https://github.com/androidx/media

issue.body:
### [REQUIRED] Issue description
MediaSessionConnector does not properly handle `play` commands from a MediaSession after a `pause` command has been handled.
If one looks at the `MediaSessionCompat.Callback.onPlay()` implementation inside `MediaSessionConnector`at [this line](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/r2.10.2/extensions/mediasession/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/ext/mediasession/MediaSessionConnector.java#L1061) it will notice that if the `Player` instance's playback state is `Player.STATE_READY` the player will not be isntructed to start playing again via `controlDispatcher.dispatchSetPlayWhenReady()` and the media session command will just do nothing. 

### [REQUIRED] Reproduction steps
The Exoplayer demo app does not post media notifications (at least I did not found a way to do it) so no direct way to reproduce it from there. Any application/code using `MediaSessionConnector` will suffice. 
The steps are:
* Initialize a `MediaSessionCompat` and make it active.
* Initialize a `ExoPlayer` instance, give it some `DataSource` that will load something to be played.
* Initialize a `MediaSesionConnector` instance with the initialized session instance.
* By using a `TransportControls` instance (can be obtained via MediaSession.getController().getTransportControls()) make an `play`action. After the playback starts, make a `pause` action.
* Try again to execute a `play` action, eventually the code form the link in the bug description will execute, and the player will be in `Player.STATE_READY` state, which will skip all if-else blocks and ignore the command.

### [REQUIRED] Link to test content
Any playable content will suffice, the bug is not about the media type, but how playback commands are handled.

### [REQUIRED] A full bug report captured from the device
No reason to post a bug report, there aren't any crashes.

### [REQUIRED] Version of ExoPlayer being used
2.10.2

### [REQUIRED] Device(s) and version(s) of Android being used
The bug involves code in a callback inside `MediaSessionConnector`, no `MediaCodec`s, no HALs or anything involved, the Android version or device is irrelevant.

body: @marcbaechinger , is it possible to just match the logic in [PlayerControlView#1232](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/release-v2/library/ui/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/ui/PlayerControlView.java#L1232)? Or maybe, just call `controlDispatcher.dispatchSetPlayWhenReady(player, true)` if the current player's state is `Player.STATE_READY`?
